title: The Declassified NASA Memo: 'We Heard a Scream From Neptune's Rings'
hook: In 1989, Voyager 2 recorded a sound from Neptune's rings that NASA classified for 30 years—because it wasn't natural.
why_this_can_go_viral: The idea of a 'scream' from space combined with a declassified document triggers instant curiosity and conspiracy interest.

title: The Extinction Event That 'Landed' in Siberia—And No One Saw It Coming
hook: Something exploded over Siberia in 1908 with the force of 1,000 atomic bombs—but no crater, no meteorite, and no explanation.
why_this_can_go_viral: The Tunguska event is a classic unsolved mystery that still terrifies people—no impact site, no debris, just destruction.

title: The Signal That 'Repeated' Every 16 Days—From a Dead Star
hook: Astronomers found a radio burst that pulses like a clock every 16 days, but the star it comes from has been dead for billions of years.
why_this_can_go_viral: A perfectly timed signal from a dead star challenges all known physics—viewers love a cosmic clock mystery.

title: The Dark Matter 'Factory' That's Creating Something in the Center of the Galaxy
hook: Something at the Milky Way's core is producing dark matter particles at an impossible rate—and it's not a black hole.
why_this_can_go_viral: Dark matter is already mysterious—suggesting a 'factory' at the center of our galaxy adds a layer of hidden danger.

title: The Rogue Planet That 'Carries' an Ocean of Liquid Diamonds
hook: A planet-sized object wandering through deep space holds an ocean of diamond—and it's heading toward a collision with a star.
why_this_can_go_viral: Diamond oceans and rogue planets are visually compelling and trigger 'what if it hit Earth' fear.

title: The Declassified KGB File: 'We Found a Structure on the Dark Side of the Moon'
hook: In 1972, a KGB satellite photographed a massive geometric structure on the far side of the Moon—the file says 'do not approach.'
why_this_can_go_viral: The Moon's dark side is a persistent conspiracy magnet—a 'do not approach' order from a secret file is irresistible.

title: The Star That 'Survived' a Supernova—And Came Out Stranger
hook: A star at the center of a supernova remnant should have been vaporized—but it's still there, pulsating in ways that break physics.
why_this_can_go_viral: A star cheating death after a supernova is a cosmic 'zombie story' that taps into primal fascination with survival.

title: The Fermi Paradox Answer: They're 'Hibernating' Until the Universe Cools Down
hook: What if advanced civilizations aren't dead—they're just waiting for the universe to become more hospitable, sleeping for billions of years.
why_this_can_go_viral: The hibernation theory is a fresh, unsettling spin on the Fermi paradox—gives viewers a 'they're still out there' chill.

title: The Asteroid That 'Turns' Into a Comet Every 5 Years—And It's Getting Closer
hook: An object in our solar system shifts between asteroid and comet as it nears Earth—and its orbit is decaying toward us.
why_this_can_go_viral: Shape-shifting space rocks are rare and scary—add a decaying orbit and viewers immediately worry about impact.

title: The Declassified US Navy File: 'We Detected a Gravity Well With No Source'

why_this_can_go_viral: Invisible gravity wells are nightmare fuel—combining military secrecy with a physics-defying phenomenon is potent.

title: The Extinction Event That 'Came From a Cloud'—And We're Passing Through It Now
hook: Earth is currently drifting through a massive interstellar cloud that may have triggered ice ages and mass extinctions before.
why_this_can_go_viral: The idea that we're already inside a death cloud is terrifyingly immediate—viewers will wonder if it's happening now.

title: The Signal That 'Came From a Planet Made of Metal'—And It's Responding
hook: Astronomers detected a radio signal from an exoplanet that's 80% metal—and when they sent a ping, it answered back.
why_this_can_go_viral: A two-way conversation with an artificial-sounding planet is every sci-fi fan's dream—and nightmare.

title: The Dark Matter 'Vortex' That's Spinning Galaxies Apart
hook: A massive dark matter vortex is ripping through a galaxy cluster, tearing stars from their orbits—and it's invisible.
why_this_can_go_viral: An invisible cosmic blender is terrifying—viewers love unseen forces that can destroy entire galaxies.

title: The Rogue Moon That 'Carries' a Magnetic Field Stronger Than Its Planet

why_this_can_go_viral: A moon stronger than its planet is a cosmic underdog story gone wrong—viewers love the 'child surpassing parent' twist.

hook: In 1979, a Soviet space probe recorded a massive object the size of a city plunging into the Sun—and it wasn't destroyed.
why_this_can_go_viral: Anything that survives the Sun is a miracle—add Cold War secrecy and it's a viral goldmine.

title: The Fermi Paradox Answer: They're 'Encased' in Simulation Shells, Unaware of Reality
hook: What if advanced civilizations don't explore space because they're trapped in perfect simulations, never knowing the real universe exists?
why_this_can_go_viral: Simulation theory is endlessly viral—applying it to alien silence adds a layer of existential dread.

title: The Extinction Event That 'Came From a Supernova'—And We Saw It 1000 Years Too Late
hook: A supernova that exploded 1,000 years ago just reached Earth—and its radiation could still trigger a mass extinction.
why_this_can_go_viral: The idea that we're only seeing a death wave after it's too late is pure horror—time delay adds dread.

why_this_can_go_viral: A vanishing megastructure near Venus combines alien mystery with government cover-up—a viral sweet spot.

title: The Declassified US Army File: 'We Tracked a Radio Signal From the Moon's Core'
hook: In 1969, Apollo 11 detected a radio pulse coming from inside the Moon—the Army classified it as 'possible subsurface intelligence.'
why_this_can_go_viral: Apollo 11 plus a secret signal from inside the Moon is the ultimate conspiracy cocktail—huge viral potential.

title: The Fermi Paradox Answer: They're 'Frozen' in Time by Relativity—We're Moving Too Fast
hook: What if aliens are perfectly still, frozen by extreme time dilation, while we race through the universe—never able to meet?
why_this_can_go_viral: Time dilation is a real physics twist that feels like sci-fi—viewers will obsess over the idea of 'frozen' aliens.
